mainTopic: Birds designated before יום טוב: when birds found the next day count as the designated ones, רוב versus קרוב, and the comparison to רבי and the חכמים on found מעשר שני money.
overview: This amud first finishes explaining why one may not handle and check birds on יום טוב itself: he might move birds that are מוקצה, or he might reject them all and lose שמחת יום טוב. Then a new משנה teaches when birds found the next morning count as the ones designated before יום טוב (הזמנה). A changed color or an extra bird makes them forbidden. A missing bird, or birds found alone in front of the nest, leaves them permitted. רבה explains that the color case refers to black and white birds that seem to have swapped places, and we assume they are new birds. The גמרא tries to prove רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב from רבה's swapped-birds case, but rejects the proof because the case is a ledge in front of the dovecote where outside birds sit, so they are close too. It then explains the counting cases and asks whether the three-became-two ruling follows only רבי, who holds in a ברייתא about מעשר שני coins that part of the money stayed and part was taken. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר answer that young birds are different because they hop, and רב אשי explains that this answer is needed for tied birds and tied pouches. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to explain how רבי would see tied pouches, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First reason why checking the birds on יום טוב is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Checking the birds by handling them is forbidden on יום טוב, because he may end up moving birds that are מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on יום טוב it is forbidden, because sometimes the birds that looked fat turn out thin and the thin ones turn out fat. Then he ends up moving something that is not fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation it started on the previous amud. Handling the birds to see which are fat is allowed on ערב יום טוב, but here it gives the first reason why this is forbidden on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only birds that were prepared before יום טוב may be moved. If he picks up a bird thinking it is fat and it turns out thin, he does not want it. That bird was never prepared for use, so he has moved מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: An object set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: But on the Festival it is forbidden,
because sometimes they are found to be
the fat ones turn out thin
and the thin ones turn out fat,
and he ends up moving something that is not fit for him.
phrases.notes: This is the problem of מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָסוּר, דְּזִימְנִין דְּמִשְׁתַּכְחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion on the previous amud about checking birds on ערב יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handling birds to check them is forbidden on יום טוב, because he may move birds he does not want, which are מוקצה.

steps.title: Second reason: he may lose out on שמחת יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Another reason: he may find all the birds thin, take none, and miss out on שמחת יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another reason: sometimes they all turn out thin, so he leaves them all. Then he ends up holding back from the joy of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate reason why checking the birds on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was about a forbidden act (moving מוקצה). This reason is about a lost good. If he is disappointed by all the birds he will eat no meat, and his יום טוב meal suffers. That is why the choosing should be done the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of rejoicing on the Festival

steps.whatToRemember: Choose and check birds on ערב יום טוב, not on יום טוב. Two reasons: (1) he might move מוקצה; (2) he might reject all of them and lose שמחת יום טוב.

phrases.english: Alternatively, sometimes
they are all found to be thin
and he leaves them all,
and he comes to hold back from the joy of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי זִימְנִין דְּמִשְׁתַּכְחִי כֻּלְּהוּ כְּחוּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason, on top of step 1, for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking on יום טוב may also cause him to reject every bird and lose out on שמחת יום טוב.

steps.title: משנה: designated birds that changed color or number
steps.stepSummary: If he designated black birds and found white ones, or the reverse, or designated two and found three, the birds are forbidden. If he designated three and found two, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he designated black birds and found white ones, or white and found black, or two and found three, they are forbidden. If he designated three and found two, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens when the birds a person designated before יום טוב look different the next morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds may only be used on יום טוב if they were designated beforehand (הזמנה). A different color means these are clearly different birds. Finding more birds than he designated means a strange bird has joined, and we cannot tell which is which. Finding fewer is fine: we assume one simply flew away, and the rest are his.

keyTerms.meaning: He designated (invited) birds before יום טוב for use on יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two number cases. Two designated and three found means forbidden, because an extra bird joined. Three designated and two found means permitted, because one just left.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he designated black ones and found white ones,
or white ones and found black ones,
or two and found three, they are forbidden.
If three and he found two, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about which birds count as the designated ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A change in color, or extra birds, makes them forbidden. Fewer birds are permitted.

steps.title: משנה: birds found in front of the nest
steps.stepSummary: If he designated birds inside the nest and found birds in front of it, they are forbidden. But if those are the only birds around, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he designated birds inside the nest and found birds in front of the nest, they are forbidden. But if no other birds are there except these, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a case about where the birds are found: outside the nest instead of inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds found outside the nest might be other birds, not the ones he designated inside. But if there are no other birds nearby at all, we assume these are his designated birds that just stepped out.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no others there except them

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹךְ הַקֵּן וּמָצָא לִפְנֵי הַקֵּן — אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: If he designated them inside the nest and found them in front of the nest, they are forbidden,
but if there are no others there except them,
these are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case about location to the משנה's cases about color and number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds found outside the nest are forbidden, unless they are the only birds there.

steps.title: Isn't the color case obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach that black birds found instead of white ones are forbidden. That seems obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first case of the משנה: designating black birds and finding white ones. Of course those are different birds, so why teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach something everyone already knows. If the birds changed color, they clearly are not the same birds. So the גמרא is looking for the real חידוש of this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the first ruling of the משנה is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that black birds designated and white birds found are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different colors obviously mean different birds, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: רבה: both colors were designated and they swapped places
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the case: he designated both black and white birds, and in the morning found the black ones where the white ones had been, and the white ones where the black ones had been.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What case are we dealing with here? He designated black and white birds. He got up in the morning and found black ones in the place of the white ones, and white ones in the place of the black ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by changing how we picture the case. This sets up the explanation of what the משנה is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה's case, both colors were designated. So finding black and white birds is not obviously wrong. The only problem is that each color is in the other's spot. Now the ruling is no longer obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Rabba said:
With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where he designated black ones and white ones,
and he got up early and found black ones in the place of the white ones
and white ones in the place of the black ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question by explaining the case differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about birds of both colors that seem to have switched places.

steps.title: The חידוש: we assume they are different birds
steps.stepSummary: One might think the same birds just switched places. The משנה teaches that we assume the designated birds left and these are new birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: these are the same birds, and they just switched places. So the משנה teaches us: those birds went off into the world, and these are other birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבה's answer by stating the mistake one might make and what the משנה teaches instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible mistake: the birds are all here and only moved around, so they should be permitted. The משנה rejects this. Since each group is not where it was left, we assume the designated birds flew away and new ones came. These new birds were never designated, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken idea)
They went off into the world

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's color case is not obvious. It refers to birds of both colors that seem to have switched places. We do not assume they just swapped spots. We assume they are new, undesignated birds, so they are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strict הזמנה is. Unless we can be confident these are the same birds that were designated, they may not be used on יום טוב.

phrases.english: You might have said:
these are the same ones
and they simply switched places,
so it teaches us:
those ones went off into the world,
and these are other ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי אִינְהוּ נִינְהוּ וְאִתְהֲפוֹכֵי אִתְהֲפוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer by stating the mistaken idea and the משנה's real lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the חידוש using the מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן structure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same birds simply switched places, so they should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume the designated birds left and these are different birds, so they are forbidden.

steps.title: Does רבה's case prove that majority beats proximity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's ruling as רבה explained it, that black and white birds found in each other's nests are forbidden, supports רבי חנינא: when רוב and קרוב conflict, follow the רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רבי חנינא, who said: when the majority points one way and the nearby source points the other way, follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the משנה's case as רבה explained it as a proof for a general rule taught by רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש״י: the black birds could be pinned on the next nest, where black birds sat yesterday, and we could say the birds just switched ('איכא למתלינהו... ולומר נהפכו'). That is proximity. The משנה instead says they came from elsewhere, from the majority of birds ('מעלמא אתו ומרובא פירשו'). So it seems the משנה follows the majority, exactly like רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say': introduces a suggested proof that may be rejected
Supports him: offers backing for someone's view
Majority: what most items in the area are
Proximity: the closest possible source of an item

steps.confusionAlert: The 'close' source here is the neighboring designated nest, which would make the birds permitted. The 'majority' is all the other undesignated birds, which would make them forbidden. Keep track of which side points to which ruling.

phrases.english: Let us say this supports Rabbi Chanina.
For Rabbi Chanina said:
When majority and proximity conflict,
phrases.notes: The case where the majority points one way and the nearest source points the other.

phrases.english: follow the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה's explanation in steps 6–7 and tries to draw a general principle from it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling, as רבה explains it, that the swapped birds are forbidden even though the neighboring nest is the nearest source

steps.title: No proof: the case is a ledge where birds from everywhere gather
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Like אביי said elsewhere, the case is a ledge (דף), where outside birds sit, so it is not a true case of רוב against קרוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said there, the case is on a ledge. Here too, the case is on a ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by saying the משנה is talking about a special place, a ledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש״י: a ledge sticks out in front of the dovecote, and outside birds sit on it all the time, afraid to enter the nests. So the outside birds are close too ('דהוו להו כלהו קרובים שבדף ושבקן'). Since proximity does not truly point to the designated birds, the משנה's ruling tells us nothing about a real conflict between רוב and קרוב.

keyTerms.meaning: As אביי said: borrows an explanation אביי gave in another place
A board or ledge sticking out in front of the dovecote, where outside birds sit
Here too: applies the same explanation to our case

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי חנינא's rule is neither proven nor disproven here. The משנה simply cannot serve as evidence for it.

phrases.english: As Abaye said: it is on a ledge,
phrases.notes: אביי said this about a different case of a bird found near a dovecote.

phrases.english: here too, it is on a ledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי בְּדַף הָכָא נָמֵי בְּדַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רבי חנינא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the found birds were truly closest to the designated nest. With outside birds sitting on the ledge right in front, they are just as close, so closeness does not point to our birds.

steps.title: Designated two, found three: forbidden either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why finding three birds where two were designated makes them forbidden. Either all are new birds, or there is one extra undesignated bird mixed in with the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Designated two and found three: they are forbidden. Whichever way you look at it: if these are other birds, then they are other birds. And if they are not other birds, there is still one extra bird mixed in with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains its reasoning with a two-sided argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the original birds flew off and these are new ones, so none were designated. Option two: the two original birds are here, but a third undesignated bird has joined them, and we cannot tell which one it is. Either way, no bird can be taken with certainty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you want': every possibility leads to the same result

phrases.english: If he designated two and found three, they are forbidden.
Whichever way you look at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַחֲרִינֵי נִינְהוּ — הָא אַחֲרִינֵי נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: if they are other birds, then they are other birds,
and if they are not other birds,
there is still one bird mixed in with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם וּמָצָא שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲסוּרִין מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the nest discussion to explaining the counting case from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Designated two and found three: all are forbidden, because either all are new birds or an undesignated bird is mixed in.

steps.title: Why are they permitted if three became two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that if he designated three and found two, they are permitted, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Designated three and found two: they are permitted. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this case is permitted. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases, any change in the birds made us suspect they were different birds. Here the number also changed, so the גמרא wants to know why we do not suspect new birds this time.

phrases.english: If he designated three and found two, they are permitted.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-to-three case to the opposite case, three-to-two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a change in the number of birds does not make us assume they are new birds

steps.title: These are the same birds and one flew away
steps.stepSummary: We assume the two remaining birds are from the original three, and that one of them simply left.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the same birds, and one of them went off into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two birds are the original ones, and the missing one just flew away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fewer birds is easy to explain without assuming anything new arrived: one simply left. More birds, as in step 10, means something new must have come in. That difference is why fewer is permitted and more is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Went off into the world (flew away)

steps.whatToRemember: A missing bird does not suggest new birds came, so the remaining birds are permitted. An extra bird proves something new arrived, so all the birds are forbidden.

phrases.english: These are the same birds,
and one of them went off into the world.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two remaining birds are the original designated ones. One bird flew away, which is a simple explanation that requires no new birds.

steps.title: Suggestion that the משנה follows only רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה follows רבי and not the חכמים, based on a ברייתא about מעשר שני money found in a different amount than was left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה follows רבי and not the חכמים. As a ברייתא teaches: If someone left a מנה (100 coins) of מעשר שני money and found two hundred, the money is חולין and מעשר שני mixed together. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: it is all חולין. If he left two hundred and found one hundred, one hundred stayed and one hundred was taken. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: it is all חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares our משנה's bird ruling to a ברייתא about coins and suggests that the משנה only fits רבי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said: designated three birds, found two, so the two are the original ones and are permitted. That is just like רבי's case of leaving 200 and finding 100, where we say 100 remained and 100 was taken. The חכמים say a changed amount means everything was replaced, so they would seem to forbid the birds. That is why the משנה looks like it follows רבי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say': the גמרא is testing a suggestion
Second tithe: produce or money that must be eaten or spent in ירושלים
One מנה stayed in place and one מנה was taken away

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction carefully. The case that matches our משנה is the second one in the ברייתא: he left MORE and found LESS, just like designating three birds and finding two.

phrases.english: Let us say our Mishnah is the view of Rebbi
and not the Rabbis,
as it is taught in a baraita:
If he left one hundred and found two hundred,

phrases.aramaic: חוּלִּין וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: ordinary money and second-tithe money are mixed together,
these are the words of Rebbi.
And the Sages say: it is all ordinary money.
If he left two hundred and found one hundred,
phrases.notes: This is the case parallel to our משנה: three birds designated, two found.

phrases.english: one hundred stayed in place and one hundred was taken,
these are the words of Rebbi.
And the Sages say: it is all ordinary money!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning of Step 12 (the two found birds are from the original three) and checks which תנא agrees with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה's ruling is accepted by everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים rule that a changed amount of מעשר שני money is all חולין, meaning everything was replaced. They would seem to reject the משנה's assumption that the remaining birds are original.

steps.title: Young birds are different because they hop
steps.stepSummary: Even the חכמים can agree with the משנה, because young birds hop around on their own, unlike coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows the חכמים. Because it was said about this משנה that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: young birds are different, since they tend to hop around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the bird case is different from the coin case, so the חכמים can agree with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins cannot move by themselves. If 100 are missing, a person took them, and that person probably took everything, as the חכמים say. A young bird can hop away on its own. So one missing bird does not suggest that the whole nest was replaced, and the remaining two are the original ones.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even if you say': introduces a way to fit the other opinion
'It was said about it': an אמורא's comment on a source

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
it was already stated about it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both say:
young birds are different,
since they tend to hop about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by showing that the coin case and the bird case are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): birds move by themselves, coins do not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to follow only רבי, since the חכמים say a changed amount means everything was replaced.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the חכמים agree with the משנה, because a missing bird probably just hopped away.

steps.title: Why is the bird answer needed, given the pouch dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the special bird answer is needed. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר limit the coin dispute to either one pouch or two pouches, and that seems to offer an easier way to fit the משנה with everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we need to answer that young birds are different because they hop? It was already said about that ברייתא that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One said: the argument is about two pouches, but with one pouch everyone agrees it is all חולין. The other said: the argument is about one pouch, but with two pouches everyone agrees that one מנה stayed and one מנה was taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 14. It suggests the משנה could fit the חכמים in a simpler way, using a dispute about pouches. Step 16 spells out this question, and רב אשי answers it in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the second view, when the money was in two separate pouches, even the חכמים agree that one pouch stayed and one was taken. Three separate birds are like separate pouches. So the חכמים would agree to the משנה anyway, and the 'birds hop' answer seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: To give an answer or explanation
'One said': introduces one side of an unnamed split between two אמוראים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. Opinion one: one pouch, everyone says חולין. Opinion two: two pouches, everyone says one מנה stayed. The challenge mainly relies on the second opinion.

phrases.english: And why do I need to answer about it
that young birds are different since they tend to hop?
But it was stated about that baraita,
by Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar,
one said: the dispute is about two pouches,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּכִיס אֶחָד — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חוּלִּין.
phrases.english: but with one pouch, everyone agrees it is ordinary money.
And one said: the dispute is about one pouch,
but with two pouches,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מָנֶה מוּנָּח וּמָנֶה מוּטָל.
phrases.english: everyone agrees one hundred stayed and one hundred was taken.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמָה לִי לְשַׁנּוֹיֵי עֲלַהּ שָׁאנֵי גּוֹזָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer in Step 14 is even needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the 'birds hop' distinction in Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חכמים agree in a two-pouch case that part stayed and part was taken, then separate birds are like separate pouches. The משנה would fit the חכמים without the hopping argument.

steps.title: The bird answer seems unnecessary under the one-pouch opinion
steps.stepSummary: The answer that birds hop works if the coin dispute is about two pouches. But under the view that the dispute is only about one pouch, and everyone agrees about two pouches, that answer seems unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says the dispute is about two pouches. That is why we needed to answer here that young birds are different, since they tend to hop around. But according to the one who says the dispute is about one pouch, and with two pouches everyone agrees that one מנה was left and one מנה was taken away, why do I need to give that answer? You said they do not argue about two pouches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out its question from step 15. The 'birds hop' answer fits one view of the coin dispute, but it seems pointless under the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two birds in a nest are like two separate pouches. If the חכמים argue even about two pouches, we need a special reason why birds are different, and 'they hop' gives one. But if everyone agrees about two pouches that one was left and one was taken, then the birds case already fits the חכמים, so the special bird answer adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (according to one view). It sets up a contrast with the next view, which does not fit as easily.
To hop or move around on their own (said of young birds)
One מנה is still in place, and one מנה was taken away

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the full spelling-out of the question raised in step 15. 'בשני כיסין לא פליגי' means everyone agrees about two pouches, so the birds case should already work for everyone.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
the dispute is about two pouches,
this is why it was necessary to answer here:
young birds are different,
since they tend to hop around.
But according to the one who says
the dispute is about one pouch,
but with two pouches, everyone agrees
that one מנה was left and one מנה was taken —
now, why do I need to answer about it?
Did you not say
that they do not argue about two pouches!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בִּשְׁנֵי כִיסִין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes the challenge begun in step 15 by laying out both views of the pouch dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 14 that birds are different because they hop.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the one-pouch view, two separate items are already treated by everyone as one left and one taken. So the birds case does not need any special reason.

steps.title: רב אשי: the case is about tied birds and tied pouches
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the case involves birds tied together and pouches tied together. Tied birds can pull free from each other, but tied pouches cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here we are dealing with birds tied together and pouches tied together. Birds can pull loose from one another, but pouches cannot pull loose from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by saying the cases involve things that are tied together. That is why the bird answer is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two pouches tied together count as 'one pouch,' so even under the one-pouch view the חכמים argue about them. Tied pouches cannot come apart by themselves, so if only one pouch is found, we assume someone took both and the one found is not the original. Tied birds can wriggle free, so one bird may have left on its own. That is why the bird distinction is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (a specific case)
They pull loose from one another

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps both parts in place: the one-pouch view of the dispute, and the need for the bird distinction. It works by placing the case in a specific setting (things tied together).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Here we are dealing with fledglings tied together
and pouches tied together.
Fledglings pull loose from each other,
pouches do not pull loose from each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָכָא בְּגוֹזָלוֹת מְקוּשָּׁרִים וְכִיסִים מְקוּשָּׁרִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under the one-pouch view, the bird answer seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tied pouches count as one pouch, and there the חכמים argue. Birds still differ because they can free themselves, so the bird answer is needed.

steps.title: How רבי would see tied pouches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain how רבי would respond about tied pouches: pouches, too, sometimes... The text breaks off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי would say to you: pouches too, sometimes...
steps.whatsHappening: There is a quiet question here. If tied pouches cannot come apart, why does רבי say one was left and one was taken? The גמרא starts to give רבי's answer, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's logic makes the חכמים look strong: tied pouches cannot separate by themselves. So רבי needs a reason why one pouch could still be missing without someone taking both. That reason begins with 'sometimes,' meaning tied pouches can also come apart in some cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי would say to you (his side of the argument)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off. The full explanation of how tied pouches can come apart comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And Rabbi would say to you:
pouches too, sometimes...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אָמַר לָךְ: כִּיסִין נָמֵי, זִמְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17, רבי's view seems hard to explain. This step starts to defend it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since tied pouches cannot separate by themselves, it seems someone must have taken both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Incomplete on this amud. Pouches, too, can sometimes come apart.
